  Tuesday, October 20, 2020 - 6:30 P.M.

Pursuant to State and County Directives, San Gabriel City Hall is closed to the public and physical access
to the meeting has been suspended. To provide members of the public access to the meeting and an
opportunity to comment on items on and off the Agenda, the following opportunities have been
established:

Public Comments

Please email all public comments to cityclerk@sgch.org and include the following on the subject line of
your email: the section (Public Comment, Consent, Public Hearing, New Business) and Item Number you
are commenting on. The Clerk will read public comments into the record for up to the three-minute limit.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will
not be read.

   City Council Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, October 20, 2020

    CALL TO ORDER
    PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Mayor Menchaca
    ROLL CALL: Mayor Menchaca, Vice Mayor Liao, Council Members Ding,
  Harrington, Pu

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. COVID-19 BRIEFING

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of October 6, 2020.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – SEPTEMBER 2020

  This is the presentation of City investments for the month of September 2020.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 20, 2020  2
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for September 2020.

  D. PHONE SERVICES PROVIDER SELECTION

  The City Council has approved up to $50,000 in funding from the 2020 Cares
  Act in an effort to upgrade the current phone system to today’s technology
  and greatly reduce expenditures and investment into the current antiquated
  phone system. An updated system will allow the City to better serve the public
  and internal workflow.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Ring Central as the City’s
  phone service provider and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement with Ring Central for phone services.

  E. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 20-54 REVISING PAY SCHEDULES FOR
  THE PERIOD OF JULY 1, 2017 THROUGH AUGUST 31, 2019

  In November 2019, CalPERS conducted an audit of the City’s authorized pay
  schedules for the period covering July 1, 2017 through August 31, 2019. The
  audit made four (4) non-material findings concerning the pay ranges listed in
  the Memoranda of Understandings (MOUs) in effect for Firefighters’
  Association (FFA), Fire Management Group (FMG), Police Officers’ Association
  (POA), and Police Management Group (PMG) from July 1, 2017 through
  August 31, 2019. Resolution No. 20-54 amends the pay ranges listed in the
  MOUs in effect for FFA, FMG, POA, and PMG from July 1, 2017 through August
  31, 2019 to clearly state and match the time base listed on the authorized pay
  schedules publicized during the same period.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Resolution No. 20-54
  amending the pay ranges listed in the MOUs for FFA, FMG, POA, and PMG in
  effect from July 1, 2017 through August 31, 2019 to address the findings
  made by the audit and bring the City’s authorized pay schedules into
  compliance with Public Employees’ Retirement Law and Public Employees’
  Pension Reform Act.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 20, 2020  3
   F. APPROVAL OF THE MEMORANDA OF UNDERSTANDING FOR A
  WORKERS’ COMPENSATION ALTERNATIVE DISPUTE RESOLUTION WITH
  THE POLICE OFFICERS’ ASSOCIATION AND POLICE MANAGEMENT
  GROUP

  Supplemental Information (Amended 10/20/2020)

  In November 2019, the Police Officers’ Association (POA) and Police
  Management Group (PMG) approached the City and requested consideration
  of a Workers’ Compensation Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) for claims
  made by the City’s sworn police personnel. ADRs provide a more expeditious
  review, treatment and dispute process for workers’ compensation claims. The
  City has come to an agreement on Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) for
  Workers’ Compensation ADRs with the POA and PMG. If approved by Council,
  the ADRs will be effective upon the date the Administrative Director for the
  California Department of Industrial Relations files the agreements.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council approve the attached Workers’
  Compensation Alternative Dispute Resolution Memoranda of Understandings
  and authorize the Mayor to execute said agreements.

  G. 2018 STATE HOMELAND SECURITY GRANT PROGRAM – RADIO
  PURCHASE

  The San Gabriel Police Department (SGPD) was awarded a grant from the
  2018 State Homeland Security Program (SHSP) in the amount of $70,199. The
  department is seeking to utilize this funding towards the purchase of 13 new
  Motorola APX 8000 portable handheld radios to enhance communications at
  SGPD and interoperability with other police agencies within the Los Angeles
  County region. This purchase will be offsetting the total cost of the radio
  communications project that will be presented to the City Council in the near
  future. If this grant funding is not used specifically for the purchase of
  portable handheld radios, the funds will be reallocated for radio
  communication purchased by other local agencies in need.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 20, 2020  4
   1. Waive formal bidding to purchase the items from Motorola Solutions
  pursuant to Municipal Code §34.34;
  2. Authorize the Police Chief to accept the 2018 SHSP grant and authorize
  the purchase of the Motorola equipment using the allocated SHSP grant
  funding;
  3. Approve to increase estimated revenue (account 186-3215) and
  appropriation (transfers out) in ‘Other Grants’ Fund by $70,199; and
  increase estimated revenue (transfers in) and appropriation in
  Capital/Special Projects Funds (account 124-751-57-99-380) by $70,199;
  and
  4. Adopt Resolution No. 20-51 accepting the Grant and terms thereof, and
  amending the Fiscal Year 2020-21 Operating Budget accordingly.

  H. SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 670
  ESTABLISHING HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS AND RELATIONS (HEAR)
  COMMISSION AND CODIFYING THE SAME UNDER CHAPTER 33
  (COMMISSIONS) OF TITLE III (ADMINISTRATION) OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE

  Ordinance No. 670 was introduced on October 6, 2020, by a 4-1 vote.
  Adoption of this Ordinance would establish a Human Equity, Access and
  Relations (HEAR) Commission and codify the same under Chapter 33
  (COMMISSIONS) of TITLE III (ADMINISTRATION) of the San Gabriel Municipal
  Code.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  670 entitled Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission.

  I. ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION APPROVING A PROPOSITION 68 –
  ROUND 4 GRANT APPLICATION AND ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION TO
  AMEND THE 2020-21 OPERATING BUDGET

  The City of San Gabriel has the opportunity to apply for grant funds through
  Statewide Park Development and Community Revitalization Program-Round
  4, funded through Proposition 68. With this final round of funding, the state
  will award over $395 million in competitive grants for the creation of new and
  renovated parks and recreation opportunities in proximity to the most
  critically-underserved communities across California. The City intends to
  apply for Statewide Park Program funding for the renovation of Smith Park

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 20, 2020  5
   and Smith Park Pool. Staff requests approval of the attached Resolution No.
  20-55 approving the City’s application for the funding. Additionally, staff
  requests approval of Resolution No. 20-66 amending the Fiscal Year 2020-21
  Operating Budget by appropriating Park Development Impact Fees in an
  amount not to exceed $22,700 to account #124-850-40-96-814.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 20-55 approving the City’s application for grant
  funds through the Proposition 68 Statewide Park Development and
  Community Revitalization Program; and
  2. Adopt Resolution No. 20-66 appropriating $22,700 from Development
  Impact Fees into account 124-850-40-96-814 for the grant expenses.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

  6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. MONTHLY BUDGET UPDATE

  The City Council unanimously passed the budget for Fiscal Year 2020-2021
  on June 23, 2020. However, due to the staggering economic impacts of
  COVID-19, the City Council requested that staff conduct a monthly update at
  the regularly-scheduled second meeting of the month. This standing item
  would be for the purposes of bringing any major changes or developments
  to the City Council.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file this report.

  B. SIXTH CYCLE REGIONAL HOUSING NEEDS ASSESSMENT (RHNA) FOR
  THE 2021-2029 PLANNING PERIOD

  Pursuant to Government Code §65584.05, any local jurisdiction within the
  Southern California Association of Governments (“SCAG”) region may file an
  appeal to modify its allocated share or another jurisdiction’s share of the
  regional housing need included as part of SCAG’s Draft Regional Housing
  Needs Assessment (RHNA) Allocation Plan (“Draft RHNA Plan”). The California
  Department of Housing and Community Development (“HCD”) may also file

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 20, 2020  6
   an appeal to one or more jurisdiction’s draft RHNA allocation. No appeal will
  be allowed relating to post-appeal reallocation adjustments made by SCAG.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and discuss the information
  contained in this staff report and provide comments and further direction to
  staff.

  C. FILM-FRIENDLY  CITY:  LOS  ANGELES  COUNTY  ECONOMIC
  DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION’S FILM-FRIENDLINESS INITIATIVE AND
  TEMPORARY FILM FEE SCHEDULE

  Being a film-friendly city has great advantages for a community: it stimulates
  local economic activity and contributes to job creation. The staff report
  identifies opportunities for the City of San Gabriel to support filming
  opportunities under the Los Angeles County Economic Development
  Corporation’s (LAEDC) Film-Friendliness Initiative, and offer temporarily-
  reduced fees for film production during COVID-19 under the 10 Point Plan
  for Recovery, Resiliency, and Reinvestment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council take following actions:

  1. Support Film-Friendliness Initiative of the Los Angeles County Economic
  Development Corporation (LAEDC); and
  2. Adopt Resolution No. 20-57 approving Temporary Film Fee Schedule as
  a part of the Economic Development 10-Point Plan.

  7. PUBLIC COMMENT

  8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members
  to report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 20, 2020  7
   11. ADJOURNMENT

  The next Regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, November 17,
  2020, at 6:30 p.m. Information regarding matters to be considered at each
  meeting will be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the
  City’s website at www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF OCTOBER 20, 2020
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

CALL TO ORDER

Mayor Menchaca called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
6:32 P.M. on Tuesday, October 20, 2020, with all Council Members and staff participating
by teleconference.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Menchaca.

ROLL CALL

Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Jason Pu, Vice Mayor
  Chin Ho Liao, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
Council Members Absent:  None.
Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City
  Manager/Community Development Director Arminé
  Chaparyan, Assistant City Attorney Lloyd Pilchen,
  Community Services/Interim Mission Playhouse
  Director Rebecca Perez, Police Chief Eugene Harris,
  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City
  Engineer Greg de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace,
  Human Resources/Risk Management Director Edward
  Macias, Interim Finance Director Kenneth Louie, and
  Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Menchaca announced the agenda order was approved.
2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. COVID-19 BRIEFING

  The presentation was made by Fire Chief Wallace and Police Chief Harris.

3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  An anonymous resident provided comments in favor of adopting Ordinance No. 670
  establishing the Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission.

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 5  October 20, 2020
   Dr. Chasity Jennings-Nuñez provide comments expressing dissatisfaction with
  comments made by Council Member Harrington regarding the formation of the HEAR
  Commission.

4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Chief City Clerk Clark stated that staff respectfully requested that item 4H, the second
  reading and adoption of Ordinance No. 670 establishing the Human Equity, Access
  and Relations (HEAR) Commission, be approved with two administrative changes.
  When the item was approved at introduction, changes were approved to remove the
  words “and scope” from proposed Municipal Code Sections 33.52(C) and 33.56(D), so
  staff requested that adoption of Ordinance No. 670 would include those changes.

  Regarding Item 4H, comments in opposition to the adoption of Ordinance No. 670
  establishing the HEAR Commission were provided by Anna Battaglia, resident; and
  Mario Pace, resident; and Isela Bowles provided comments expressing concerns
  related to the formation of the Commission.

  Vice Mayor Liao pulled Item 4I for separate discussion.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Council Member Pu, to approve
  Consent Calendar Items 4A – 4G as presented, and Item 4H as amended per staff’s
  request as detailed above.

  Motion approved Consent Calendar Items 4A – 4G as presented and Item 4H as amended
  by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  Regarding Item 4I, in response to questions from Vice Mayor Liao, Community
  Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Perez provided details about the grant
  process.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Mayor Menchaca, to approve
  Consent Calendar Item 4I as presented.

  Motion approved Consent Calendar Item 4I as presented by a vote of 5-0 as follows:
  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of
  October 6, 2020.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved the September 25, 2020, and October 1, 2020, Registers
  of Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – SEPTEMBER 2020
CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 5  October 20, 2020
   The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for September
  2020.

  D. PHONE SERVICES PROVIDER SELECTION

  The City Council approved Ring Central as the City’s phone service provider and
  authorized the City Manager to execute the agreement with Ring Central for phone
  services.

  E. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 20-54 REVISING PAY SCHEDULES FOR THE
  PERIOD OF JULY 1, 2017 THROUGH AUGUST 31, 2019

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 20-54 amending the pay ranges listed
  in the Memoranda of Understandings (MOUs) with the Firefighters’ Association
  (FFA), Fire Management Group (FMG), Police Officers’ Association (POA), and Police
  Management Group (PMG) in effect from July 1, 2017, through August 31, 2019, to
  address the findings made by the audit and bring the City’s authorized pay
  schedules into compliance with Public Employees’ Retirement Law and Public
  Employees’ Pension Reform Act.

  F. APPROVAL OF THE MEMORANDA OF UNDERSTANDING FOR A WORKERS’
  COMPENSATION ALTERNATIVE DISPUTE RESOLUTION WITH THE POLICE
  OFFICERS’ ASSOCIATION AND POLICE MANAGEMENT GROUP

  The City Council approved the Workers’ Compensation Alternative Dispute
  Resolution Memoranda of Understandings and authorized the Mayor to execute
  the agreements.

  G. 2018 STATE HOMELAND SECURITY GRANT PROGRAM – RADIO PURCHASE

  The City Council:

  1. Waived formal bidding to purchase the items from Motorola Solutions
  pursuant to Municipal Code §34.34;
  2. Authorized the Police Chief to accept the 2018 SHSP grant and authorized the
  purchase of the Motorola equipment using the allocated SHSP grant funding;
  3. Approved an increase to estimated revenue (account 186-3215) and
  appropriation (transfers out) in ‘Other Grants’ Fund by $70,199; and increased
  estimated revenue (transfers in) and appropriation in Capital/Special Projects
  Funds (account 124-751-57-99-380) by $70,199; and
  4. Adopted Resolution No. 20-51 accepting the Grant and terms thereof, and
  amending the Fiscal Year 2020-21 Operating Budget accordingly.

  H. SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 670 ESTABLISHING
  HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS AND RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION AND
  CODIFYING THE SAME UNDER CHAPTER 33 (COMMISSIONS) OF TITLE III
  (ADMINISTRATION) OF THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE

  The City Council waived reading and adopted Ordinance No. 670 establishing the
  Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission under Chapter 33
  (COMMISSIONS) of TITLE III (ADMINISTRATION) of the San Gabriel Municipal
  Code.

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 5  October 20, 2020
   I. ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION APPROVING A PROPOSITION 68 – ROUND 4
  GRANT APPLICATION AND ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION TO AMEND THE
  2020-21 OPERATING BUDGET

  The City Council:

  1. Adopted Resolution No. 20-55 approving the City’s application for grant
  funds through the Proposition 68 Statewide Park Development and Community
  Revitalization Program; and
  2. Adopted Resolution No. 20-66 appropriating $22,700 from Development
  Impact Fees into account 124-850-40-96-814 for the grant expenses.

5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. MONTHLY BUDGET UPDATE

  The staff presentation was made by Interim Finance Director Ken Louie.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included allocation of the Athens contract-extension revenue and any
  surplus revenue; appreciation for the increased detail in the Budget Updates;
  street-paving needs; and financial uncertainty during the COVID-19 crisis.

  The City Council received and filed the report.

  B. SIXTH CYCLE REGIONAL HOUSING NEEDS ASSESSMENT (RHNA) FOR THE
  2021-2029 PLANNING PERIOD

  The staff presentation was made by Planning Manager Samantha Tewesart.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included costs to file an appeal; transit-oriented housing and job
  centers; effects of remote-working on the housing market; upcoming affordable-
  housing projects in the City; consequences of not meeting RHNA requirements and
  alternative ways to comply with State law through the City’s Housing Element and
  zoning; failure of past appeals; successful appeals resulting in other communities
  having an increased number of units allotted; methodology for allocation; higher-
  density future projects; upcoming Housing Element update; and filing an appeal as
  a defensive measure in case other cities file appeals.
  There was a consensus of the City Council to direct staff to file an appeal of the
  allocated RHNA units-number for the City.

  C. FILM-FRIENDLY CITY: LOS ANGELES COUNTY ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
  CORPORATION’S FILM-FRIENDLINESS INITIATIVE AND TEMPORARY FILM
  FEE SCHEDULE
  The staff presentation was made by Economic Development Manager Domenica
  Megerdichian.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included that additional services provided by the City would be billed
  separately; this is a temporary fee schedule while a fee schedule study is being

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 5  October 20, 2020
   conducted and during the pandemic; alignment with FilmLA for marketing and fee
  structure; the value of Historic sites to filmmakers; getting input from the Historic
  Preservation and Cultural Resources Commission; filming-permit details; this item
  is the first of several film initiatives; and past filming activity in the City.

  A motion was made by Council Member Ding, seconded by Vice Mayor Liao, to:

  1. Support the Film-Friendliness Initiative of the Los Angeles County Economic
  Development Corporation (LAEDC); and
  2. Adopt Resolution No. 20-57 approving the Temporary Film Fee Schedule as a
  part of the Economic Development 10-Point Plan.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:
  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

7. PUBLIC COMMENT – None.

8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT – None.

9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Council Member Pu reported on his attendance of the virtual League of California
  Cities Annual Conference where he was appointed First Vice-President of the Asian-
  Pacific Islander (API) Caucus; and on the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments
  (COG) Governing Board meeting where he was elected as Chair of the Transportation
  Committee.

  Council Member Ding reported on his attendance of the virtual California Joint Powers
  Insurance Authority (CJPIA) Annual Conference.

  Vice Mayor Liao announced that Athens Services will give away free compost on
  October 24, 2020, from 9:00 A.M. – 12:00 P.M. at Vincent Lugo Park.
  Mayor Menchaca reported on her attendance of the virtual League of California Cities
  Annual Conference.

10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

11. ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Menchaca adjourned the meeting at 8:42 P.M.

Respectfully submitted:

_____________________________________
JULIE NGUYEN, City Clerk

Approved this 17th day of November, 2020:

_____________________________________
DENISE MENCHACA, Mayor
CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 5 of 5  October 20, 2020
